name: Text to SQL
title: Text to SQL
answer: Text to SQL is the task of translating a natural language question into a SQL query that runs against a real schema and returns the answer. It sits between AI and SQL, and it is how business users query data without an analyst in between. The scope covers question understanding, schema linking, query generation, execution, and sometimes result explanation. It applies to relational databases and warehouses, not to every data store.

It sits between AI and SQL, and it is how business users query data without an analyst in between. The scope covers question understanding, schema linking, query generation, execution, and sometimes result explanation. It applies to relational databases and warehouses, not to every data store.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Text to SQL systems run on a database engine, commonly PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks, plus a language model that generates the query. The model may be hosted in a cloud API or run locally, and the database connection is usually read only for safety. Tooling often includes a schema catalog, a query validator, and an execution sandbox. The site tracks 263 Model Context Protocol servers for SQL databases and warehouses out of 2451 active servers, which shows how common this integration pattern has become.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical pipeline starts by retrieving the relevant tables and columns from a schema catalog, then prompts a language model with the question, the schema, and a few examples. The model writes a SQL candidate, which is parsed and checked against the schema before it runs. If execution fails or returns an unexpected shape, the system may retry with the error message or ask a clarifying question. Some systems use fine tuning or retrieval augmented generation to improve accuracy on large schemas.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Text to SQL carries risks of wrong answers, leaked sensitive columns, and queries that are expensive or destructive. Provenance matters because a generated query should be traceable to the schema version, the model, and the prompt that produced it. Access controls, row level security, and read only roles are common safeguards. Teams also log queries and results for audit, and they review generated SQL before it reaches production data.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward agentic workflows that inspect schemas, run queries, and correct themselves without a human in the loop for every step. Benchmarks and research continue to push accuracy on complex joins and ambiguous questions. Integration with Model Context Protocol servers is making it easier to connect language models to databases and warehouses. The long term goal is reliable self service analytics, but human review will remain important for high stakes data.
